validate: cites no passage: Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, "Existing Letters of Credit" means each letter of credit issued by a Lender in its capacity as an "Issuing Bank" under the Existing 2004 Five-Year Credit Agreement for the account of the Borrower that is outstanding on the date of the agreement (September 28, 2005) and is identified in writing by the Borrower to the Administrative Agent as an Existing Letter of Credit on or before that date.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement between Tyson Foods and the Administrative Agent, the Borrower must promptly furnish notice of all actions, suits and proceedings before any court or other Governmental Authority affecting the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries which, individually or in the aggregate, has any reasonable likelihood of having a Material Adverse Effect.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement, the Administrative Agent must promptly furnish to the Lenders the notices described in clauses (a), (b) and (e) of Section 6.10, other than in the case of clause (d) and, other than to the requesting Lender, clause (e).

The Five-Year Credit Agreement dated September 28, 2005 embodies the entire agreement and understanding among Tyson Foods, Inc. as Borrower, the Lenders, and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as Administrative Agent, and supersedes all prior agreements and understandings of such persons relating to its subject matter, except for the Fee Letter and any prior arrangements made with respect to the payment by the Borrower of (or any indemnification for) any fees, costs, or expenses payable to or incurred by or on behalf of the Administrative Agent or the Lenders.

Citicorp USA, Inc., represented by Richard M. Levin as Director, signed the Five-Year Credit Agreement dated as of September 28, 2005 among Tyson Foods, Inc., the lenders party thereto, and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as Administrative Agent.
validate: too long for one fact: Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, if, other than as provided in Sections 3.05, 3.08, 3.09, 3.10 or 3.11, any Lender obtains any payment, whether voluntary, involuntary, through the exercise of any right of set-off or otherwise, on account of any Committed Loan made by it and, after acceleration of all Obligations pursuant to Section 8.02(b), in respect of any Obligation owing to it including with respect to any Bid Loan, in the case of the Committed Loan in excess of its Percentage Share of payments on account of the Committed Loans obtained by all the Lenders and, after acceleration, in excess of its pro rata share of all Obligations, such Lender shall forthwith notify the Administrative Agent of that fact and purchase from the other Lenders such participations in the Committed Loans made by them or, after acceleration, in all Obligations owing to them, as shall be necessary to cause the purchasing Lender to share the excess payment ratably with each of the other Lenders according to their respective Percentage Shares or, after acceleration, their pro rata shares of all the Obligations.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, the Borrower agrees to reimburse each Lender and hold each Lender harmless from any loss, cost or expense incurred as a consequence of (a) any failure of the Borrower to borrow, continue or convert a Eurodollar Loan after giving a Notice of Borrowing or Notice of Conversion/Continuation, (b) any prepayment or payment of a Eurodollar Loan on a day that is not the last day of the applicable Interest Period, (c) any failure of the Borrower to make a prepayment after giving notice under Section 2.07, (d) conversion of a Eurodollar Loan to a Reference Rate Loan on a day that is not the last day of the Interest Period under Section 2.10, or (e) assignment of a Eurodollar Loan other than on the last day of the Interest Period as a result of a Borrower request under Section 3.13, including losses from liquidation or reemployment of funds or fees to terminate deposits.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement between Tyson Foods (as Borrower) and the lenders, permitted asset dispositions include: the sale or disposition of inventory and farm products in the ordinary course of business; the sale or disposition in the ordinary course of business of assets that have become obsolete or surplus to the business of the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries, or have no remaining useful life, as reasonably determined in good faith by the Borrower or such Subsidiary; the periodic sales to third parties of live inventory and related products and services under grow out contracts; Permitted Dispositions; the sale or disposition of Permitted Investments; the sale of accounts or other receivables by the Borrower and its Subsidiaries in connection with the Receivables Facility or to a special purpose bankruptcy remote Subsidiary or a third party for not less than fair value, without recourse (other than to any such special purpose Subsidiary), in connection with a receivables purchase transaction; and the sale or disposition of Excess Margin Stock for not less than fair value.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, the Borrower may not enter into or permit any of its Subsidiaries to enter into any agreement that prohibits, limits or restricts repayment of loans, advances or other distributions to the Borrower by any Subsidiary, or that restricts any Subsidiary's ability to declare or pay dividends or other distributions on its capital stock or to acquire or make payments in respect thereof, except for restrictions imposed by law or by the agreement, restrictions existing on the date of the agreement identified on Schedule 7.09 (which exception does not apply to any extension, renewal, amendment or modification that expands the scope of such restriction), and customary restrictions in agreements relating to the sale of a Subsidiary pending such sale, provided the restrictions apply only to the Subsidiary being sold and the sale is permitted under the agreement.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement between Tyson Foods and the Administrative Agent, the Borrower agrees to indemnify, defend, reimburse and hold harmless the Administrative Agent, the Syndication Agent, each Documentation Agent, each Co-Documentation Agent, each Lender, each Issuing Bank and each of their Affiliates, and each of their respective directors, officers, employees, agents and advisors (each an Indemnified Party) from and against all claims, actions, proceedings, suits, damages, losses, liabilities, costs and reasonable expenses, including the reasonable fees, charges and disbursements of counsel (including the allocated cost of in-house counsel), incurred by or asserted against any Indemnified Party in connection with, arising out of or relating to (i) any transaction or proposed transaction (whether or not consummated) financed or to be financed, in whole or in part, directly or indirectly, with the proceeds of any Borrowing or otherwise contemplated in the Five-Year Credit Agreement, (ii) the entering into and performance of the Five-Year Credit Agreement and any other Loan Document by the Administrative Agent, the Syndication Agent, any Documentation Agent, any Co-Documentation Agent or any Lender or Issuing Bank or any action or omission of the Borrower in connection therewith, or (iii) any investigation, litigation, suit, action or proceeding (regardless of whether an Indemnified Party is a party thereto) which relates to any of the foregoing or to any Environmental Claim, unless and to the extent such claim, action, proceeding, suit, damage, loss, liability, cost or expense was solely attributable to such Indemnified Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct as determined by a final judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction.
decision_floors.grounded: The Five-Year Credit Agreement includes a Leverage Ratio covenant and an Interest Expense Coverage Ratio covenant.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, "Consolidated Net Income Available for Restricted Payments" equals the sum of $150,000,000 plus 80% (or minus 100% in case of consolidated net loss) of Consolidated Net Income for the period commencing October 3, 2004 and terminating at the fiscal quarter end of the Borrower immediately preceding the date of any proposed Restricted Payment.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, "Priority Debt" means any Indebtedness secured by a Lien (including in connection with capital leases or other financing leases) encumbering any asset of the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries.
Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, "Priority Debt" means any sale-leaseback transaction involving assets of the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries.
Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, the Receivables Facility must be in full force and effect as a condition to the effectiveness of the agreement.
decision_floors.atomic: The Five-Year Credit Agreement includes a Leverage Ratio covenant and an Interest Expense Coverage Ratio covenant.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement, "Solvent" means, with respect to any Person, that the fair value of that Person's assets (both at fair valuation and at present fair saleable value) is greater than the total amount of its liabilities including contingent and unliquidated liabilities, that the Person is able to pay its liabilities as they mature, and that the Person does not have unreasonably small capital with which to carry on its business.

Under the Financing Agreement of Life Sciences Research between the Parent, the Agent and the Lenders, there are no outstanding debt or equity securities of the Parent or any of its Subsidiaries and no outstanding obligations convertible into or exchangeable for, or warrants, options or other rights for the purchase or acquisition from the Parent or any of its Subsidiaries, or other obligations of any Subsidiary to issue, directly or indirectly, any shares of Capital Stock of any Subsidiary of the Parent.

Under the First Amendment to the Life Sciences Research Financing Agreement, the Guarantors and the Borrower release the Lender Parties from all claims, whether known or unknown, fixed or contingent, secured or unsecured, arising out of or relating to the Amendment, the Financing Agreement, any other Loan Document, and related transactions and agreements, based on acts or omissions occurring at or prior to and including the date of the Amendment.
decision_floors.useful: Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, "IRS" means the Internal Revenue Service of the United States of America.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, "Person" means an individual, partnership, corporation, business trust, joint stock company, trust, unincorporated association, joint venture or Governmental Authority.
Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement, "US Dollars" or "US$" refers to lawful money of the United States of America.
Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement, the word "includes" and "including" are not exclusive and mean "includes, without limitation" and "including, without limitation".
Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, the headings are inserted for convenience only and do not affect the meaning or interpretation of the agreement or any of its provisions.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, "Priority Debt" means any sale-leaseback transaction involving assets of the Borrower or any of its Subsidiaries.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement of Tyson Foods, the Administrative Agent must receive, together with TFM's executed counterpart of the Guarantee Agreement, such documents and certificates as the Administrative Agent or its counsel may reasonably request relating to the organization, existence and good standing of TFM and the authorization of the Transactions to which TFM is party.
Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement, a Permitted Lien includes any Lien created pursuant to any Loan Document.

Under the Five-Year Credit Agreement, a Permitted Lien includes Liens for taxes, assessments or governmental charges or levies either not yet due and payable or the non-payment of which is permitted by Section 6.03.
decision_floors.distinct: Under the amended Applicable Rate definition in the Tyson Foods Five-Year Credit Agreement, a change in the Moody's or S&P ratings of the Index Debt (other than from a change in the rating system) is effective as of the date the change is first publicly announced by Moody's or S&P.

Under the amended Applicable Rate definition in the Tyson Foods Five-Year Credit Agreement, if the Moody's and S&P ratings for the Index Debt fall within different categories, the Applicable Rate is based on the higher rating, unless the ratings differ by two or more categories, in which case the Applicable Rate is based on the category one level below the higher rating.

Under the amended Applicable Rate definition in the Tyson Foods Five-Year Credit Agreement, if the rating system of Moody's or S&P changes or either agency ceases rating corporate debt, Tyson Foods, Inc. and the Lenders must negotiate in good faith to amend the definition, and pending such amendment the Applicable Rate is determined by the rating most recently in effect before the change or cessation.

Under the amended Applicable Rate definition in the Tyson Foods Five-Year Credit Agreement, each change in the Applicable Rate applies from the effective date of that change until the day before the effective date of the next change.

Under the Amendment 1 to the Furniture Brands Note Purchase Agreement, the Company will not permit any Subsidiary that is not an Obligor to become a borrower or a guarantor of Indebtedness owed to banks under the Credit Agreement unless such Subsidiary is, or concurrently becomes, a party to the Subsidiary Guaranty.
